title: I found this sub recently, mind if I share?
content: It is all very interesting, I am of spaniard descent, for me, it is a city built entirely on classic architecture, but big. Picture the pisa tower, but as high as the empire state, with all the arches, balconies, half-bubble tops? (I don't know how they are called in english). Bóbedas, cúpulas. I find myself walking on the street, I can see the shadows of the buildings making a pattern on the ground, I can touch the stone columns, they are not entirely smooth, like, they have those tiny holes when they get old?. I look up, I can see people on the balconies, a hundred levels up, they look tiny, there are pots with plants hanging down, flowers, with a bunch of colours, windows fold up to open, like those roman style wooden thingies. People around me (on the ground) are dressed like spaniard equivalent to eduardian / victorian clothing, cars are not very consistent? like old timey but ranging from carriages with horses all the way to 1950's. Well that's downtown, where the big stuff is. Suburbs are weird,same buildings, but only 3 to 5 levels up, I see more green areas than downtown, streets have those grassy divides in between the lanes? with larger trees on then, the branches are wide, and they go over the lanes, so cars ride under the shadowplay of the branches. It seems like the further from downtown I go, the buildings go down in levels, but they look the same style, and more and larger green areas, people riding their old timey bicycles, old timey hmmm, 'shoes with wheels'? The outskirts of the city are strait up spanish contryside. Sometimes I go inside the buildings, they look as expected from such architecture. Ok, so technology is present but it is bonkers, people carry cellphones, but they look like seashells, the concave side is like a mirror or screen, where they see or read the info. It feels like they are ... scrying?. I go there often, but It does not stick to my memory for longer that a few hours, as soon as I get to daily routine, they leave. This is obviously not my mother language, so excuse my attempted writing. Laters.
